title: Midweek bridge brief — Aug 11 2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick midweek sync and triage for platform-engineering. Short (~30m) readout to the broader eng org; capture decisions and action items to unstick ongoing rollouts.

Attendees:
Sofia Alvarez (owner), Ethan Park, Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor, Janelle Park, Andy Ruiz (observer) + ops on Slack thread #bridge-midweek

Top-line summary:
- Small but notable SLO drift on hosted-api p95 latency for text-generation (model: redwood-3b-mix) across us-east-1 during Monday spike — investigation shows degraded batching efficiency after feature flag change.
- Dedicated pools: autoscaler regression (INF-2048) caused a delayed horizontal scale by ~3 minutes under load test; mitigations underway and hotfix PR opened.
- Cost pulse: token-processing cost increased ~12% week-over-week for a subset of customers due to a config change that disabled prefix caching for older clients; we have a mitigation roadmap and communications plan.
- Canary rollout for quantized-7b-v2 paused after an unexplained 0.6% quality regression on the eval set (small sample) — rollout hold, expanded eval, and rollback plan discussed.

Metrics snapshot (last 24h):
- Hosted API p95 (text-gen): 320ms -> baseline 270ms (18% increase during spike windows)
- Serving runtime CPU eff: 64% avg (target 60%)
- Dedicated pool scale latency (scale-up): median 24s -> regression spike to 3m under peak in one test cluster
- Costs (selected customers): +12% tokens processed; unit cost per 1k tokens up from $0.98 -> $1.10 for impacted cohort

Incidents & root-cause notes:
1) Latency drift (Monday spike) — root cause candidate: batching/control-plane handshake introduced in feature flag FF-5315. On inspection, a race caused some requests to bypass the continuous-batching queue and hit the low-efficiency path. Temporary mitigation: revert FF-5315 for affected clusters (deployed), longer-term follow-up: add end-to-end test that simulates interleaved small/large requests (owner: Ethan).
2) Autoscaler lag (INF-2048) — caused by a bad backoff config and an off-by-one in pod readiness check. Hotfix PR #856 opened, rolling to staging now (owner: Priya).
3) Prefix caching disabled for legacy clients — a config rollout inadvertently included an opt-out that should have been gated. Patch rolling to re-enable caching for clients older than v1.4 is planned (owner: Janelle). Communication to impacted customers drafted by CS (linked).

Decisions made in this sync:
- Pause canary for quantized-7b-v2 until expanded eval completes (decision owner: Liam).
- Immediate revert of FF-5315 in us-east-1 and us-west-2; leave feature gated in non-prod until tests pass (decision owner: Sofia).
- Approve emergency hotfix for autoscaler backoff (ship after green CI and one successful staging smoke test) (decision owner: Priya).
- Minor changes to rollout checklist: add client-config audit step and a caching validation for every deploy touching request-path (owner: Janelle).

Action items (owners + due):
- Ethan: Add E2E test for mixed-size batching scenarios; include synthetic traffic generator by Aug 18.
- Priya: Merge autoscaler hotfix PR (#856) and coordinate staging run; report status by EOD Aug 12.
- Janelle: Patch to re-enable prefix-caching for legacy clients and prepare CS message; staging rollout Aug 13, customer notify draft by Aug 13.
- Liam: Run expanded eval for quantized-7b-v2 over 10k prompt set, include A/B QA and edge case suite; results due Aug 14.
- Sofia: Draft postmortem skeleton for the latency drift incident, collect logs and sampling plan; initial draft Aug 15.

Cross-team spotlights & blockers:
- Observability: new tracing tags shipped last week helped isolate few malformed headers; however, logs retention default change (obs-config-12) is causing gaps for some long-tail traces. Observability team to revert retention tweak for prod by Aug 13 (owner: Andy).
- Solutions Eng: needs confirmation of rollback windows for a small enterprise customer on Dedicated to avoid overlap with their own maintenance — action: Priya to coordinate.

Communication plan:
- Customer Success will notify affected customers for caching incident by Aug 13; message drafted and under review.
- Platform status: internal all-hands note with incident summary and link to postmortem skeleton (Sofia) scheduled for Aug 16 planning cadence.

Risks & notes:
- If the quantized-7b re-eval shows no regression, we will validate canary with a narrowed traffic slice only (5% traffic) and extended quality monitoring for 48h.
- Autoscaler hotfix must be validated under both steady ramp and burst patterns; failing to cover both may leave us vulnerable to the next load test.

Parking lot (deferred discussion items):
- Revisit global routing fallback policy (cost vs latency tradeoff) — propose a short design doc next week (owner: TBD).
- Longer-term: explore prefix-caching telemetry to make cache misses per-customer visible in dashboard (obs + optimize).

Appendix: quick links
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/856
- Jira tickets: INF-2048 (autoscaler), INF-2101 (canary quality regression), INF-2133 (prefix caching)
